items.feedback: You picked a, a string at the top of call.py. The slip is that the string is part of the file, so pushing call.py to GitHub publishes your key along with it. The correct answer is b: the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable lives in your shell, and the SDK reads it by itself, so the code can be shared without it. Reread the first paragraph of "Make the call" in lessons/0001-one-model-call-from-python.html, looking for where the key lives and who reads it.

Yes, c is right, and it's an instinct to trust. max_tokens is a rev limiter: it only cuts in at the top, so a short answer ends on its own with stop_reason "end_turn". To see the other case, rerun step 6 ("Predict, then run") of "Demo: one call, then a conversation" in lessons/0001-one-model-call-from-python.html.

You picked a, and the first half is right: your program does have to append the earlier answer. It goes wrong at the role, because "user" tells the model that you said those words. The correct answer is d, role "assistant": the role records whose words they are, even though your code does the typing. It's tempting to think only the model can write assistant turns, but the model never touches your list. Reread "A second mix-up" under "The API remembers nothing" in lessons/0001-one-model-call-from-python.html, looking for who writes the assistant dicts.

You picked d, and the first slip is in answer = reply.content: that takes the content field, while stop_reason is a separate field that these lines never touch. The correct answer is a: content is a list of blocks, and a Python list has no .upper(), so the second line fails. You have to pull the string out of a text block before you can use string methods on it. Reread "A common mix-up" under "Demo: one call, then a conversation" in lessons/0001-one-model-call-from-python.html, looking for what type reply.content is.

Your 30 matches the three questions (3 × 10), so if that's how you got it, you were right that earlier questions are sent again. It first goes wrong right after question 1: ask() also appends the 50-token reply as an assistant turn, and the same happens after question 2. The correct answer is 130 tokens, because both earlier replies travel with the three questions; this is the same gap as q3. Reread Figure 2 in "The API remembers nothing" in lessons/0001-one-model-call-from-python.html, and label each box in the call 3 row with its tokens.

summary: 1 of 5. You have max_tokens as a ceiling (q2). You also didn't pick "the API already holds the earlier answer" this time, which is a step forward from your first quiz. The thing to work on next is what's inside the history: your program saves each reply as an assistant turn and resends it (q3, q5). Two smaller fixes are keeping the key out of the file (q1) and knowing that reply.content is a list of blocks (q4). Next step: run steps 2 to 5 of "Demo: one call, then a conversation" in lessons/0001-one-model-call-from-python.html, print messages before each call and say whose words each dict holds, then reread "Make the call" and "The API remembers nothing". After that, try a fresh quiz on O1, since you've now seen this one's answers.
